text: What does mogging mean: Collins word of the year 2026. Mogging is slang meaning to outshine or outperform someone or something. Collins English Dictionary named it its word of the year for 2026, and the term is used mainly by Gen Z and Gen Alpha, the younger generations.. Collins English Dictionary announced "mogging" as its 2026 word of the year, after the word's usage rose 210% during 2026. The announcement came in a press release issued on a Tuesday.. Collins said usage of the word rose 210% during 2026. Its lexicographers monitor about 27 billion words a year, and the dictionary's managing director, Alex Beecroft, said the choice shows how each generation leaves its mark on language. The word is believed to come from "AMOG," short for "alpha male of the group." Its first use was as a noun in bodybuilding circles, where it named the most physically dominant man in a gym. It later became a verb and was briefly taken up by the manosphere. Collins's writer Rachel Quin dates its first appearance in bodybuilding to about 2016. Other shortlisted entries included "hydration break," "Manchesterism," "ghost job," "carspreading," "firewave," "friendslop," "fricy," "bixie" and "P(doom)." Quin described the list as "one big mogging contest," since many of the terms compare one thing against another.

What is a ballot curing period? Mail ballot fix window explained. A ballot curing period is a window of time in which a voter whose mail ballot has a problem can supply missing information or confirm a signature so the vote is counted. These ballots are often the last ones tabulated, so the period can delay final totals in close races during the 2026 midterm election count.. The 2026 midterm elections will take hours, days or weeks to finish counting in some races, and election officials in each state run their own counts. Curing periods are one reason some close contests take longer to call.. Some states give voters a set number of days after election day to fix a mail ballot that has a defect, such as a signature that does not match the one on file. The voter is given a chance to provide additional information or verify the signature, and the ballot is then counted if the fix is accepted. Because these ballots are processed last, the curing period can keep a race uncounted for days after the polls close. The rule matters now because all 435 House seats, 33 Senate seats and 36 governor's offices are on the ballot this year. Many key races are expected to be close, and CBS News has noted that close races tend to be decided later. Some states also count mail ballots postmarked by election day for days afterward, and the US Supreme Court has upheld that practice, so late-arriving ballots can also extend the count. A result is still not final when the curing period ends. Local authorities must canvass and certify the totals, and very narrow margins, usually a fraction of a percent, can trigger an automatic recount under state or local law.

What is same day voter registration? California's Oct. 19 cutoff. Same day voter registration is a process that lets an eligible citizen sign up to vote at a polling place or election office on or near Election Day, after the normal registration deadline has passed. In California, a voter who uses it casts a provisional ballot, which is counted once officials confirm eligibility.. Registration deadlines for the Nov. 3, 2026 midterm elections have passed in many states, including New York (Oct. 24), New Jersey (Oct. 13) and California (Oct. 19 for online registration). Same day registration is the remaining route for some voters in those states.. The online registration deadline for the Nov. 3, 2026 general election in California was Oct. 19. Under California's process, a person who missed that date can register as a conditional voter at a county elections office, a polling place or a vote center, within 14 days of the election or on Election Day itself. Applicants need a state driver's license or California identification card number, or the last four digits of a Social Security number. Anyone without these can still register and will receive a unique identifier. In New York, the deadline for the 2026 midterms was Oct. 24, and New Jersey's was Oct. 13. New York allows registration during early voting, and because the registration deadline and early voting both fall 10 days before the election, there was one day when residents could both register and vote. Residents of New York who register on Election Day cannot cast a regular ballot in this election unless they met the Oct. 24 deadline. The rules differ by state, which is why the question is in the news now. Voters who missed their state's deadline should check their county election office for whether same-day registration is available to them.

What is california Proposition 12: the pork rule behind the Iowa Senate fight. California Proposition 12 is a California state law that sets minimum space and housing standards for certain farm animals, such as breeding pigs, raised for meat sold in California. Because it applies to products sold in the state, it reaches farms in other states, including Iowa. Its rules are now a central issue in the Iowa Senate race.. With Election Day days away, the Iowa Senate race between Josh Turek and Ashley Hinson is close, and the two have clashed over Proposition 12 and the Save Our Bacon Act. Turek said at a Grinnell farm visit that he would not back the bill.. Proposition 12 is a measure California voters approved that sets rules for how certain livestock are housed. The rules cover the space given to animals such as hogs and the kind of enclosures they may be kept in. The law applies to meat and other animal products sold within California, so out-of-state producers who want to sell into that market must meet its standards as well. Iowa is among the largest pork-producing states, and many Iowa hog farms ship products to other states. For that reason, the law affects farmers far from California. Some lawmakers have proposed federal bills to limit how far state rules like this can reach across state lines. One such proposal is the Save Our Bacon Act, introduced by Ashley Hinson, the Republican who represents Iowa's 2nd Congressional District. It was written in response to California's law. What is the Save Our Bacon Act: Hinson's Iowa hog bill explained. The Save Our Bacon Act is a proposed federal bill introduced by Republican Ashley Hinson, U.S. Representative for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District. It would prevent individual states from applying their own rules to meat and other livestock products shipped into them from other states. The bill was written in response to California's Proposition 12, a set of animal-housing standards.. Josh Turek, a Democratic state representative, said at a farm near Grinnell, Iowa, that he would not support the bill, which his Republican opponent Ashley Hinson has championed in the tight Iowa Senate race. The race could affect which party controls the U.S. Senate.. Hinson introduced the measure as a response to California's Proposition 12, which sets standards for how animals such as hogs are raised. Under the bill, a state could not use its own rules to restrict the sale of products produced in another state. Supporters say it would protect Iowa hog producers from having to meet California's rules to sell there. The bill is now a central issue in the Iowa U.S. Senate race. Hinson is the Republican nominee, and her opponent, Democrat Josh Turek, a state representative, has said he would not back it. Turek said the measure mainly helps large, international companies, naming JBS Foods and Smithfield Foods, and that it does little for small Iowa farmers. He said he would support country-of-origin labeling and other help for small pork and beef producers instead. Farmers disagree about who benefits. Hog farmer Linda Schroeder of northwest Iowa said small family farms cannot pay the roughly $3,000 per sale that compliance with Proposition 12 would cost, and that the bill would help them. The Hinson campaign said Turek "has no idea what he's talking about" on agriculture and Proposition 12. Election Day is four days after the Grinnell farm visit, and polling averages show the race nearly tied, with Hinson slightly ahead.

What happened in Itaewon crowd crush 2022: Halloween disaster in Seoul. The Itaewon crowd crush was a deadly disaster on Halloween night in 2022 in Itaewon, a nightlife district in Seoul, South Korea. Tens of thousands of partygoers surged in narrow alleys, and nearly 160 people died. It has returned to the news because of footage from it used in a video game.. Activision said it will remove footage of the Itaewon disaster from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 after objections from victims' families. The change comes days before the fourth anniversary of the disaster on October 29.. Itaewon is a nightlife district in central Seoul, the capital of South Korea. On the evening of October 29, 2022, a very large crowd, reported by sources as more than 100,000 people, gathered there to celebrate Halloween. The alleys were so crowded that people could not move, and some could not breathe. The crowd surged beyond control in a narrow alley, and nearly 160 people died. Families of the dead say the victims included people who performed CPR on one another while others lay on the cold street. After the disaster, an investigation into the failure of authorities to prevent it began. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged, and three former police officers have been jailed. The investigation is still underway. Families of victims say they are still waiting for answers. In late October 2026, the American publisher Activision said it would remove about 10 seconds of news footage of the disaster from the opening of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The game depicts a fictional North Korean invasion of South Korea. Families of victims called the use of the footage inappropriate, and Activision apologized, saying it had never meant to trivialize the disaster. The removal is scheduled for a game update on November 12. The families welcomed the removal but said they had received no direct apology. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said his government would uncover the truth about the disaster.
